_comment: Live Music starter (ship plan P4, 2026-11-27). Public and generic: asks the person's city, what they like and which venues they go to, then makes one page of this week's shows that they can keep private or share at mchatai.com/u/<their id>/<slug>/. The deterministic half is live-music/tools/events.py (linked into the working folder by workdirLinks): it reads each venue's own calendar, keeps the week, checks every show the assistant adds by hand against the saved venue page, and renders the page. Runs on the person's Mac (Rule #2). Nothing about any one person or city is in this folder.
blurb: Tell it your city and the venues you like; it makes a page of this week's shows, every one linked to the venue.
_whyCadenceManual: The legacy cadence job composes a calendar-and-sources brief, which is not this assistant's work, and per-assistant schedules are not built (ASSISTANT_SDK_ARCHITECTURE AS.4; routines.* agent verbs are not in the app yet). The person asks for this week's page; CONTEXT.md says so plainly instead of promising a schedule.
_whyRecords: Venues are a series, so they are ROWS of 'Live Music Venues' (Key = venue name; Calendar URL, Neighborhood, Notes), never memories (the CW.4 job-search lesson). Memories hold only the person's city and what they like. The Ledger table also outlives a thread's working folder, so a new thread rebuilds venues.json from it.
_whyQualityControl: evidence: every show on the page links to the venue's own listing, and a show the assistant read by hand is kept only if its title and link are on the venue page saved in week/pages/ (events.py on_page). deterministic: events.py, not the model, decides the week, the times it read from the venue's own data, duplicates and which picks exist. human: sharing to mchatai.com is hub.deploy, which the person approves.
_whyFreshness: Each week's page is rebuilt from the venues' calendars as they stand that day; nothing carries over, so there is nothing to repeat. No schedule trigger either.
_whyToolsEnumerated: No wildcards: hub.unpublish deletes a page for good, and aiweb has write verbs this assistant never needs (proposeActions, captureForAssistant). hub.deploy is kind external, so each share is an approval card unless the person chose Allow All.
_whyBudget: Advisory, checked only when another assistant relays a question here. One weekly page is a handful of turns; reading venue pages by hand is the expensive part.
